This release involved transferring seven files to the production server: five landing-page update-notice files, the version file that triggers distribution, and a progress-log file. The transfer itself succeeded completely, and the production site confirmed it was showing the new vers…

articles.author: Lerat
articles.description:
I Built a Design Skill to Make AI-Generated Websites Less Generic — FireBall v3


AI can generate a website in seconds.
But there's a problem: a lot of AI-generated websites end up looking the same.
The same rounded cards.
I wanted to change that.
FireBall is an open-source design skill designed to help AI coding and design agents create interfaces that feel more intentional and adapted to the project.
Instead of forcing every project into the same visual style, FireBall focuses on understanding the context of the design and giving the AI more freedom to make appropriate decisions.
v3 is now available.
The main improvements are:
Denser designs — more information and stronger layouts without automatically making the interface messy.
More design freedom — fewer rigid constraints and more room for the AI to adapt.
Better adaptation — the design can better reflect the product, its purpose, and its visual direction.
The goal isn't to make every AI-generated website look different just for the sake of being different.
The goal is to make the design feel like it was actually designed for the project.
Two upcoming versions are officially planned:
A dedicated version focused on Image-to-Website, with a complete system specifically designed for turning visual references into websites.
More freedom in the design process, giving the AI even more room to make creative decisions.
There are also ideas for a v4, including a larger restructuring of the skill, overall improvements, and better generated designs.
However, v4 is not officially announced yet.
FireBall is open source, and you can check out the project here:
https://github.com/Lerat-tlmnul/Fireball-DesignSkill
I'd love to hear feedback from developers and designers.
Does giving AI more design freedom actually produce better interfaces? What would you change?
I'm still working on FireBall, and v3 is only the beginning. 🔥
articles.title: I Built a Design Skill to Make AI-Generated Websites Less Generic — FireBall v3

Give an AI agent a Git token and a Kubernetes ServiceAccount. Now ask which team owns it, and where its logs go. If you cannot answer both in one breath, congratulations: you have shadow AI in your pipeline. Bisi's working definition is uncomfortably broad on purpose: shadow AI is any AI tool, model, agent, extension, or integration used in the software lifecycle without formal approval, ownership, risk assessment, or monitoring. The assistant writing your commit messages is one thing. The agent holding a token that can push to main, or a ServiceAccount that can restart a workload, is…

articles.author: ai maya
articles.description:
A year ago, connecting a model to your tools meant writing glue for that model, in that framework, with that vendor's function-calling format. Swap the model and you rewrote the glue. In 2026, that pain is mostly gone, and the reason has a boring name: the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
MCP is worth understanding not because it's clever, but because it's winning — and the reason it's winning tells you where the industry's center of gravity is moving.
Strip away the branding and MCP is a small client–server contract for connecting language models to the outside world. A server exposes three kinds of things: tools (functions the model can call), resources (data the model can read), and prompts (reusable templates). A client — your IDE, your agent, your chat app — speaks the same protocol and …
articles.title: MCP in 2026: How the Model Context Protocol Became the USB-C of AI Tooling

articles.author: Q00
articles.description:
Most AI coding tools fail before they write a single line of code. The prompt was vague, and the model quietly filled the gaps with assumptions you never agreed to.
You ask for "a task management CLI." The model picks a data model, a priority scheme, a persistence layer — all reasonable, none of them yours. You find out three files in, during review, and you rework it. That's the loop most of us are stuck in: prompt, guess, rework, repeat.
Ouroboros is an open-source Agent OS that fixes the input instead of the output. It's a local-first runtime layer that sits in front of Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Kiro, Hermes, Pi, and Zcode, and replaces ad-hoc prompting with a five-stage, replayable workflow: interview, seed, execute, evaluate, evolve.
